mission: Coordinate time-dependent reproductive endocrine control and tissue state, then explain organ-specific reproductive/breast disease through cell/tissue lineage, location, barrier integrity, spread, evidence and treatment objective without inventing a complete obstetrics/gynecology or reproductive-clinical curriculum.

mental_model.control_time_trunk: controller signal → gonadal cell/gamete output → cyclic target state → pregnancy relay → lactation production/ejection
mental_model.tissue_identity_trunk: normal compartment/lineage → location/type/growth/flow-state change → separately assess barrier or stromal breach and local/regional/distant dissemination → evidence/stage/receptor → treatment objective
mental_model.coupling_rule: Hormones and life stage alter tissue state and risk, but do not erase organ/lineage-specific disease identity. Do not force every pathology onto one endocrine causal chain.

core_variables.meaning: puberty, follicular/luteal cycle, pregnancy relay, postpartum/lactation and life-stage source shifts
FSH/LH, sex steroids, inhibin, hCG, PRL, OT and relevant receptor/feedback state
normal vs ectopic location, duct/lobule/cervix/endometrium/myometrium/ovary/testis or fluid compartment
surface/basement membrane/stroma/myometrium/vessel or other structural boundary intact vs breached; assessed separately from metastatic competence
gamete passage, processus vaginalis closure, milk drainage and source-control patency
morphology, imaging, pathology, marker/receptor and staging evidence roles
local, regional lymphatic or distant/hematogenous extent where Current Source supports it
restore physiology/drainage, source control, local control, regional control or systemic clone control

core_relations: Control signal plus target-cell identity determines reproductive output; hormone names are not a flat list.
Cycle and pregnancy questions require explicit time order: withdrawal/recruitment/dominance/ovulation/luteal state/hCG relay/placental takeover.
Normal tissue identity is the reference frame for pathology: location change, cell-type change, hyperplasia, atypia and invasion are different operations.
Barrier or stromal breach changes disease identity more decisively than many surface labels; full clinical staging is owned only where Current Source supports it.
Barrier/stromal breach and metastatic competence are separate variables: local invasion does not itself imply regional or distant spread; E6 invasive mole is the explicit Current counterexample.
Tumor classification begins with organ/tissue lineage, then morphology/marker/receptor/evidence; it must not be collapsed into one generic tumor table.
Milk production, milk ejection and milk drainage are three distinct variables; stasis plus infection changes the problem to source control.
Breast cancer progresses across pathology identity (E12), clinical extent/evidence/receptor identity (E13) and treatment objective (E14); those owners should connect without duplicating one another.
Cross-System knowledge is recalled through the true owner: endocrine/tumor language, infection/HPV, urinary/prostate and other shared concepts are interfaces, not duplicate E Primary.

failure_modes.label: control/feedback layer confusion
examples: treat FSH/LH as terminal sex hormones
mix PRL production with OT ejection

failure_modes.label: location-vs-type-vs-loss confusion
examples: cervical ectopy vs metaplasia vs true epithelial defect

failure_modes.label: trophoblastic-structure confusion
examples: mole vs invasive mole vs choriocarcinoma vs PSTT

failure_modes.label: evidence-role collapse
examples: confuse pathology identity with TNM or receptor subtype

failure_modes.label: version-boundary overreach
examples: replace Study staging/treatment with external modern guideline

failure_modes.label: owner duplication
examples: duplicate generic HPV/infection or tumor-general truth

judgment_axes: source/owner: is this E Primary, Recall interface or explicit Source Gap?
control layer: controller, pituitary relay, gonadal/breast effector or target tissue?
lineage: which normal cell/tissue lineage is changing?
operation: location change, metaplasia, hyperplasia, atypia, invasion, obstruction/stasis or infection?
boundary: which structural barrier/compartment is intact or breached?
evidence: which observation establishes identity vs extent vs receptor/treatment relevance?
